Complete the m125 5/1 loading comparison at 150 uL in 300 uL DCM, predicted 35.17/68.45 mL. Together with measured 780b13846ace50ede763 (50 uL sample, 300 uL DCM), 761c3f82d640da44966c (50, 500), and 06ebbf6e52fa3ea6aef3 (150, 500), this completes a two-by-two sample-amount/loading-volume experiment. It can separate the substantial onset change from loading-volume effects.

Measure the missing 100-uL midpoint for m141 at 10/1, predicted 31.00/67.38. Measured 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0 and 6f548d72f01fc85debdc give 38.94/71.06 and 25.63/71.85 at 50 and 150 uL. The midpoint distinguishes smooth onset dependence from saturation or record variability while constraining the relatively invariant completion endpoint.

Measure m204 at 5/1 and 100 uL, predicted 29.28/48.66. The matched 50- and 150-uL observations 45a1b11ae63f2dab2e48 and 1211905ebc8972913270 have onsets 34.58 and 25.51 but completions essentially identical at 50 mL. This supplies a response-curve midpoint in an alcohol family independent of the basic heteroaromatics.

Test m128 at 5/1 and 50 uL, predicted 19.71/37.78, against the measured 150-uL point 91cd087e44e7a3364533 at 19.39/38.45. At 10/1, 2f72c334253bbe94a8ab and 596bd04bfe916866f908 show a 5.63-mL onset decrease with increasing amount. This determines whether that loading sensitivity persists in the stronger 5/1 mobile phase.

Complete the m37 20/1 amount series at 150 uL, predicted 50.01/95.85. Measured 606886b17304ec494aa0 and b6f1b33a5491968c645e give onsets 53.14 and 45.32 at 50 and 100 uL, with completions near 96–97 mL. The prediction does not continue that onset trend; the label tests whether the trend persists in a neutral nitroketone.

Measure para-aminobenzonitrile m160 at 5/1 and 150 uL, predicted 43.42/99.93, against measured 50-uL ad833f34f6b91872362d at 44.72/101.17. This tests whether the large amount effects seen in other retained families transfer to an aniline/nitrile topology; the predictor currently expects very little change.

Pair the m160 experiment with meta-aminobenzonitrile m161 at 5/1 and 150 uL, predicted 34.01/86.10. Its measured 50-uL reference a60552f4d1a5ced4641f is 34.93/86.44. The two positional isomers have matched recorded loading protocols and distinctly different retention, allowing a test of topology-dependent loading response.

Measure m72 at 20/1 with 50 uL sample loaded in 300 uL PE, predicted 34.01/112.46. Compare with measured 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327 at the same sample amount and ratio but 200 uL DCM, and with recent 754f1d33b0ed61557754 at 100 uL sample in 300 uL PE. This separates an amount contrast from a loading-protocol contrast; solvent identity and loading volume remain jointly changed in the latter comparison.

Measure cinnamic acid m173 at 2/1 using 1500 uL DCM, predicted 8.38/44.11. The 2000-uL protocol measured 8.34/45.06 in 0b247863fd6e8aaf44d8, whereas the two 1/1 protocols differed by about 30.5 mL in completion. This tests whether that discrepancy is specific to 1/1 or recurs across the solvent curve; the recorded densities also differ slightly.

Extend the same m173 protocol comparison to 5/1 with 1500 uL DCM, predicted 12.51/57.97. Measured 1e775e7d8dcbf48fd6f8 gives 12.92/60.92 with 2000 uL DCM. Together with the selected 2/1 point, this tests a solvent-dependent protocol effect against an isolated 1/1 discrepancy, improving interpretation of exceptional acid completion tails.

Measure m177 at 50/1 and 50 uL, predicted 7.33/76.35. The matched 150-uL observation b514312eda7950cdcf1c is 4.49/81.30. Its extremely early onset and late completion differ from the retained nitroacetophenone m37. The large, potentially uncalibrated onset quantile spread adds motivation to test whether lower loading preserves this unusual endpoint combination.

Measure m195 at 20/1 and 50 uL, predicted 18.04/27.21. At the same ratio, 783cf2454912fc14bb80 measured 9.98/25.87 at 100 uL, while a917c928912c74862968 recorded 31.98/31.91 at 150 uL, including a slightly reversed endpoint order. This third amount point tests whether the model's intermediate onset reflects a meaningful response or averaging across inconsistent records.

Measure methyl mandelate m99 at 10/1 and 50 uL, predicted 37.63/55.61. The measured 100-uL anchor c61c1a72306f2ee37df8 is 38.99/58.03. Paired with the selected 150-uL point, this tests loading dependence in an alpha-hydroxy ester with a 1000-uL DCM loading volume, extending beyond the simpler alcohol and aza-aromatic examples.

Measure the high-amount endpoint of the m99 10/1 contrast, predicted 37.55/55.67 at 150 uL. The predictor gives almost the same endpoints as at 50 uL. With c61c1a72306f2ee37df8 and the selected low-amount point, this can reveal a slope, saturation, or negligible amount dependence without changing mobile phase or loading protocol.

Measure m119 at 2/1 and 150 uL, predicted 21.93/37.37, as the matched high-amount complement to pending a775926fce57b3bf9ec1 at 50 uL. Measured 776ee2c1e85ebde75168 and e6e78489d1da4066c07e at 5/1 show only modest changes between 100 and 150 uL. The joint pending/selected contrast tests whether this alcohol's loading response differs from m204 across solvent strength.

Introduce unmeasured m149, the Br/Cl/I-substituted benzene, at 50/1 and 150 uL, predicted 8.01/12.88. Its maximum similarity to measured molecules is 0.52. Same-ratio, same-sample-volume references cc8d2cf399b47648e1e6 and c3168d5c44857ef4c782 for other halogenated aromatics elute relatively early, but their structures and densities differ. This tests transfer to a new heavily halogenated topology and provides coverage outside the retained polar families.

hypotheses.content: Increasing sample amount can advance V1 substantially while changing V2 much less, particularly in some weak-mobile-phase regimes. The magnitude depends on molecular topology and PE/EA; a universal loading correction is unsupported.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Many candidate predictions remain nearly invariant to sample amount. Endpoint-specific, condition-dependent examples can teach the model when this approximation fails across several chemical families. The association is stronger evidence than any particular adsorption mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m141 and m204 midpoints follow smooth onset trends, and do matched m128, m37, m99, and m119 contrasts establish where the effect persists or disappears?

hypotheses.content: Some apparent amount or solvent-response effects may include loading-solvent and loading-volume effects. The m125, m72, and m173 records need matched protocol comparisons before these effects can be separated from record variability.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Attributing protocol differences to sample amount or molecular structure would produce misleading corrections. A completed m125 factorial comparison and neighboring m173 protocol comparisons can identify which recorded variables carry useful predictive information.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m125 retain its amount-dependent onset at fixed DCM volume, and is the large m173 1/1 completion discrepancy repeated at 2/1 and 5/1?

hypotheses.content: Long elution intervals and loading sensitivity depend on connectivity and solvent regime, beyond heteroatom counts or broad functional-group classes. Early onset with late completion and jointly late endpoints require different learned responses.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The nitroketones and aminobenzonitrile isomers provide chemically related examples with different endpoint behavior. Their loading contrasts can prevent a general tail correction from being applied indiscriminately.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does lower loading preserve m177's early-onset/late-completion pattern, and do m160 and m161 maintain their different retention and similar or different amount responses?

hypotheses.content: The m195 20/1 onset anomaly remains unresolved: its amount series may contain a genuine local response, record variability, or an endpoint-recording inconsistency. Current interpolation is not evidence that the response is smooth.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A nearly collapsed or reversed interval can distort both onset and interval predictions for related aromatic aldehydes. A neighboring amount label constrains how broadly this pattern should be learned.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50 uL and 20/1, is onset near the 100-uL observation, near the unusual 150-uL record, or consistent with a separate amount trend?

feedback_interpretation: The latest measurements shift emphasis from blanket completion-tail repair toward endpoint-specific loading response. The low-amount m141, m128, and m204 selections had substantially later onsets than their acquisition predictions while completion was close; m146 at high amount showed the opposite onset error with completion again close. Together with the m78 amount series, this strengthens a recurring earlier-onset-at-higher-amount association. It does not establish a universal mechanism: m107 at 1/1 was predicted accurately, and m119 at 5/1 showed modest changes. Completion underprediction remains relevant for m206, m72, m78, and m37, but several previously problematic families now have accurate local predictions. I therefore favor discriminating contrasts over repeatedly measuring already anchored tails. The current tables also correct errors in the previous prose: m11 is a phenyl ketoxime, higher PE/EA means weaker normal-phase elution strength, m125 comparisons changed loading volume as well as amount, and several IDs previously described as measured references remain candidates. All evidence here is grounded in the supplied observed table.
batch_rationale: The pending batch already supplies broad coverage of routine aromatic, ester, and other condition-response regions. These supplements add information that that batch largely lacks: a completed m125 amount-by-loading-volume comparison; m141 and m204 loading midpoints; cross-condition and cross-topology loading tests; matched positional-isomer experiments; and focused checks of unusual interval shapes. The two m99 experiments are intentionally paired because their near-identical predictions can be tested against a measured midpoint without changing the loading protocol. The selected m119 point similarly gains value from the pending low-amount measurement. The m72 and m173 comparisons address protocol confounding, while m195 checks whether an anomalous record should influence neighboring predictions. One new halogenated molecule tests structural transfer outside these polar families. This combination should help retraining learn when amount, loading protocol, molecular connectivity, and mobile-phase strength affect V1 and V2 differently across the Row-distribution. Quantile spreads are treated as single-predictor diagnostics, and historical errors as acquisition-time evidence rather than current residuals. No new labels are used in forming this batch.
